title: Peopling of Sahul
summary: Anatomically modern humans cross the Wallacean straits to the Pleistocene continent of Sahul.
detail:
Archaeological evidence from northern Australia pushes occupation back to c. 65,000 years ago.

Ancestors of Aboriginal Australians and Papuans were among the first maritime travellers.
debate: Dates of 65,000 BP at Madjedbebe are contested; some argue for 50,000 BP.

title: Austronesian expansion out of Taiwan
summary: Austronesian-speaking farmers and seafarers move south from Taiwan into the Philippines and beyond.
detail:
Linguistic, archaeological and genetic evidence converge on a Taiwan homeland for the Austronesian family.

Within 1,500 years the language family stretched from Madagascar to Easter Island.

title: Indic court culture reaches the Mekong delta
summary: Sanskritic kingship, script and religion arrive with Indian Ocean traders.
detail: Port cities such as Oc Eo linked the South China Sea with the Bay of Bengal.

title: Srivijaya and Buddhist maritime networks
summary: A Malay-speaking thalassocracy controls the straits and hosts Buddhist scholars.
detail:
Yijing visited in 671 CE and recorded over a thousand monks.

The polity's centre is debated.
debate: Whether Srivijaya was centred at Palembang or Jambi-Muara Takus remains disputed.

title: Melaka and the spice trade
summary: Melaka becomes the entrepôt of the Malay world before falling to the Portuguese.
detail:
Pepper, cloves and nutmeg moved through the port.

Islam spread along these networks.
